references.title: The Discovery and Orbit of 1993 (243)1 Dactyl
references.facts: Non-unique mass-dependent orbital family, encounter position near 85 km and speed near 6 m/s. Table IV identifies encounter states in J2000 at 1993-08-28 16:52:04.66 UTC. Numeric Dactyl table rows have not been acquired/visually verified in this intake; they are not implementation-ready states.

references.title: Dactyl: Galileo Observations of Ida’s Satellite
references.facts: Published full principal diameters 1.6 × 1.4 × 1.2 km; longest axis approximately toward Ida and shortest approximately perpendicular to orbital plane. These constrain an approximate encounter attitude, not a measured contemporary rotation solution.

references.title: Galileo’s Encounter with 243 Ida: An Overview of the Imaging Experiment
references.facts: Dactyl rotation rate is unknown; the long-axis alignment suggests synchronism but does not prove it.

references.title: Dactyl Dark Side Illuminated by Idashine
references.facts: Confirms original field-edge clipping, approximately 24 m/pixel, faint reflected illumination from Ida. The press representation shifts the edge inward and enhances the dark side: use original pixels for registration.

comparisonWithSelam.encounterState: Stronger published route: original orbit work identifies a family of J2000 state vectors at an explicit 1993 epoch. Exact rows remain to be acquired and independently transcribed.
comparisonWithSelam.attitude: The published parent-axis and orbit-normal alignments constrain a model, but these two original frames have not established a unique full attitude or uncertainty covariance. The I2700 clipping and low dark-side signal weaken the second silhouette constraint.
comparisonWithSelam.currentPhase: No defensible current phase found. The original authors explicitly could not determine a unique orbit. A single family member propagated to 2026 would be an unsupported prediction.
